memory_update.text: LEU should remain the benchmark public reference name for HALEU/enrichment exposure; later layers should test scale, contract durability, and whether valuation already discounts bottleneck control.
BWXT belongs in the reference lane for advanced fuel fabrication, especially TRISO, but its exposure is mixed with broader nuclear components, naval nuclear, and services businesses.
HON maps to US uranium conversion via Honeywell Metropolis/ConverDyn, but it is a diluted mega-cap exposure rather than a clean conversion trade.

ASPI is a Serenity underfollowed/speculative-shadow candidate for proposed HALEU enrichment, but survival into later layers requires hard evidence on licensing, technical demonstration, funding, and customer contract enforceability.

node: Uranium conversion, enrichment, HALEU production, and advanced nuclear fuel supply
summary: Layer 1B expansion for this node finds very few clean public-market expressions. Centrus Energy is the clearest US-listed HALEU/enrichment reference name; BWX Technologies is the most credible public advanced-fuel and TRISO fabrication name; Honeywell is the hidden mega-cap conversion exposure via the Metropolis/ConverDyn channel; ASP Isotopes is an underfollowed but high-risk speculative shadow candidate tied to proposed HALEU enrichment and supply agreements. The main Serenity takeaway is that the bottleneck appears real, but public exposure is narrow, often oversized, or dependent on licensing, government funding, technical execution, and reactor-customer qualification.
